transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Dr. Leah Brooks (Zenith Head of ML), Marcus Lin (Zenith Platform Eng), Priya Das (Zenith SRE)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in to align on new capacity top-up, adding APAC region for burst capacity, and contract term extension to cover discounted committed units. Goal to scope pilot benchmarks and agree next steps for procurement.

Topics:
- Current usage & forecast (p95/p99, RPS spikes)
- APAC burst region onboarding and data residency considerations
- Contract amendment: term extension vs month-to-month top-up pricing
- Security: KMS, SOC2 audit cadence, VPC peering
- Pilot benchmarks and timeline

Action items (recorded in notes above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, we, uh, really appreciate you making the time. quick roll call?
[00:08] Leah: Leah here, hi.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus, on platform.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:14] Carlos: Carlos from Redwood, SE.
[00:16] Samira: awesome. quick agenda—sync on the renewal numbers, talk about APAC burst region, and then next steps for pilot. sound good?
[00:24] Leah: yep sounds good. our execs are keen to lock down pricing and the apac plan this quarter.
[00:30] Marcus: just to flag, our traffic has this weird bimodal daily spike because of support flows, so we want a solution that's cost-effective but can handle 8x bursts.
[00:40] Samira: got it, thanks. can you give a quick rundown of current committed units and where you see growth?
[00:47] Marcus: sure. we're at 500k tokens/day committed, peak day of about 4m tokens. projections show a 2.5x increase over next 12 months if pilot in APAC goes well.
[01:01] Carlos: when you say peak of 4m, is that steady or sub-minute spikes?
[01:06] Marcus: mostly sub-minute spikes, like 30–90s bursts when the chat agent fans out across customers.
[01:13] Priya: and our p95 latency requirement is 180ms for the user-facing flows, otherwise product sees degradation. p99 can be leaky at 350ms but not great.
[01:25] Samira: okay that helps frame the routing options—dedicated vs hosted plus burst. for APAC we can do a hybrid: localdedicated pool for low-latency plus hosted fallback for overflow.
[01:37] Leah: localdedicated? do you mean dedicated GPU nodes in ap-southeast?
[01:42] Carlos: yes, ap-southeast region dedicated pool that you reserve capacity for, and then we have host fallback to reduce cold starts. sorry, our transcript system keeps messing with terms—it's dedicated pool in ap-southeast and hosted overflow in our global catalog.
[01:55] Marcus: sounds reasonable. cost wise what's the delta? we've got procurement concerns.
[02:00] Samira: the committed dedicated pool is more cost-effective for sustained throughput, about 20–30% less per token at your volumes, but you need a ~12 month commit to access the discount tiers. the burst/overflow uses our hosted fleet at on-demand rates.
[02:14] Leah: given that, execs want a 12-month extension if the math lands. can we get an amendment that shows breakpoints? like 500k–1m, 1m–2.5m, 2.5m+.
[02:25] Samira: yep we can model tiered pricing in the SOW. i'll include breakpoints and a hypothetical spend table.
[02:30] Priya: security questions—our security team asked about KMS integration and key rotation, and whether Redwood supports HSM-backed keys.
[02:38] Carlos: we do support customer-managed keys via KMS and can integrate with HSM providers. we also provide audit logs for key usage. small caveat: some on-prem HSMs need a network path for enrollment; we can work with your infra on that.
[02:54] Marcus: also need to confirm SOC2 status and whether there's an annual audit report we can get.
[02:59] Samira: yes, we're SOC 2 Type II, and we can share the attestation and a redacted report under NDA. i'll attach that to the SOW packet.
[03:08] Leah: great. two more blue-sky things—data residency: for APAC we need to ensure PII never leaves region. is that possible?
[03:15] Carlos: yes, we can lock traffic to the ap-southeast geocluster and enforce routing policy that prevents egress. for hybrid fallbacks we can ensure sensitive payloads are routed to the private VPC/dedicated pool only. there is some nuance with third-party tool calls if you have them.
[03:30] Marcus: we do have a small set of external analytics calls that touch hashed ids — should we be worried?
[03:36] Carlos: those calls can be proxied through your VPC or we can apply data-masking at the SDK layer; both are common patterns.
[03:43] Samira: ok back to capacity: for the pilot we propose a 4-week benchmark across eu and apac: week 1 baseline run eu, week 2 baseline run apac, week 3 stress runs, week 4 soak and integration tests. does that timeline map to your ops windows?
[03:58] Marcus: yes, that should work. prefer the stress runs in our off-peak at 02:00 local time so it doesn't clash with customer traffic.
[04:06] Priya: can we run a KV cache validation too? last time we saw cache thrash under certain prompt patterns.
[04:12] Carlos: absolutely—we'll include KV cache hit/miss metrics and a recommended cache sizing config. note: our KV cache tuning can change p99 by up to 40% on shaped workloads.
[04:22] Leah: wonderful. procurement note—if we sign for 12 months, do you offer rollover credits or true-ups if usage spikes?
[04:30] Samira: we have two options: committed units with monthly true-up at discounted overage rates, or committed + reserved burst credits that you can apply. i'll put both on the table in the SOW.
[04:41] Marcus: sounds good. also curious about upgrade lead time—if we want to provision a new dedicated pool in apac how long does that take?
[04:48] Carlos: typical lead time is 5–7 business days for standard configs, up to 2 weeks for custom SKUs or on-prem packaging.
[04:56] Priya: do you support private control plane in the APAC region? we may need on-prem later.
[05:02] Carlos: yes, Private deployments are an option; for APAC we'd discuss either VPC-private control plane or an on-prem appliance. timelines there are longer—usually multi-week to coordinate networking and KMS.
[05:14] Leah: procurement will want to see a sample amendment. also, do you provide SLA credits for downtime?
[05:20] Samira: yes, Dedicated comes with SLA targets and credits tied to availability thresholds. i'll include typical SLA language and example credit calculations.
[05:29] Marcus: can we get a short TCO calc for two scenarios: 12-month commit vs 6-month commit + higher overage?
[05:36] Samira: yep, we'll run those numbers and include a TCO sheet.
[05:40] Priya: one more ops ask—if we need to swap model variants mid-run for cost reasons, how does rollbacks/rollouts look?
[05:48] Carlos: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. you can pin model versions and we expose rollout metrics in console so you can watch latency and error rates. rollback is instant to previous pinned version.
[05:59] Leah: good. competition check—Megacloud AI said they'd offer a similar regional cache product for free for 3 months. how do we position?
[06:07] Samira: total cost of ownership and reliability is our pitch. we also provide the operational runbook, KV tuning and SLA backed dedicated nodes; Megacloud's free tier may be fine for a quick spike but might not give you p95 guarantees.
[06:20] Marcus: agreed. okay, what's the next step to get procurement rolling?
[06:25] Samira: i'll send a revised SOW and a pricing sheet with tier breakpoints by 2027-09-10. i'll cc legal with the sample SLA and SOC docs.
[06:32] Leah: and we'll aim to confirm traffic histograms and signoff by 2027-09-12.
[06:37] Priya: and we'll do the security review with our infosec—i'll send a calendar invite for 2027-09-14.
[06:43] Carlos: i'll prep the benchmark artifacts and an initial runbook—expect that by 2027-09-18.
[06:49] Samira: perfect. any outstanding blockers?
[06:52] Marcus: procurement asked for sample invoice and payment terms—net45 ok?
[06:57] Samira: we can do net45 for enterprise deals, i'll flag ops to include payment term options in the SOW.
[07:03] Leah: great. small note—we also want to validate key rotation window during the benchmark so no surprises.
[07:09] Carlos: we'll include key rotation test steps in the runbook.
[07:13] Priya: one tangent—if we later move to on-prem, will the same rollout policies work?
[07:19] Carlos: yes same API and rollout semantics. private deployments preserve feature parity for rollouts, though some observability hooks need extra config.
[07:28] Samira: ok closing notes: Samira to send SOW + pricing + SOC2 by 9/10, Marcus to share histograms by 9/12, Priya to schedule infosec review 9/14, Carlos to deliver benchmark runbook 9/18.
[07:44] Leah: thanks everyone.
[07:46] Marcus: thanks.
[07:47] Priya: bye.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional words corrected where system garbled product names (e.g., 'localdedicated' normalized to 'dedicated pool'). Some technical terms transcribed phonetically (K-V cash instead of KV cache) but clarified during call.
